previous_delivery.name: Micro Zoom logo
previous_delivery.used: The title screen, the pause menu header and the library card.
previous_delivery.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: ONE finished transparent PNG game asset. Visual style for the game Micro Zoom: a Victorian natural-history laboratory seen through clean modern editorial design. Brass microscope fittings, engraved scale rules and vernier marks, aged ivory paper, specimen-slide labels, copperplate details, deep ink green, oxblood and brass accents, soft natural light. Scientific and a little steampunk, never technological: no screens, no holograms, no neon, no circuitry. A game title logo: the words "MICRO ZOOM" in capitals, spelled exactly M-I-C-R-O Z-O-O-M, in an elegant engraved serif with brass inlay and a thin ink outline, the O of ZOOM drawn as a microscope objective lens seen end-on with concentric brass rings and a tiny tardigrade silhouette inside. A fine engraved scale rule underlines the words. Wide landscape composition, even margins, no other text, no watermark. Transparent background (PNG with alpha). If transparency is not possible, use a flat pure magenta #FF00FF background with nothing else on it and no cast shadow; it is keyed out on integration.
Shared visual vocabulary: finely engraved antique BRASS, dark ink-green and warm ivory accents, Victorian naturalist cabinet, precise restrained ornament. REAL alpha transparency, not a painted checkerboard, no magenta fallback. Output wide5:2. The ONLY text is MICRO ZOOM, exactly these nine letters with one space. Set it on ONE HORIZONTAL LINE with generous clear alpha margin on all sides. Keep all letters readable and evenly spaced. Replace the FIRST O in ZOOM with a brass objective ring containing a tiny eight-legged tardigrade silhouette, preserving the O silhouette; the second O remains an engraved serif O. One thin engraved scale rule below, tiny ticks with NO numerals. No subtitle, badge, banner, extra text or background. Supplied organisms are anatomy references only, do not paste their photographic surroundings.
